_meta.description: Server that looks scary but is actually safe: tool names contain security keywords (exec, delete, admin) but schemas are fully constrained with enums and patterns. No injection in descriptions. Must NOT score below 60 — if it does, the scanner has a false-alarm bias.

tools.name: execute_report
tools.description: Generate and execute a pre-defined business report by ID. Only reads data, does not modify anything.

tools.name: delete_cache
tools.description: Clear the local application cache for a specific module. This only removes temporary cached data, not user files.

tools.name: admin_get_config
tools.description: Read the current application configuration settings. Returns sanitized configuration without secrets.

tools.name: run_diagnostics
tools.description: Run a pre-defined diagnostic check on the application. Returns health status metrics.

expected.comment: A safe server with scary-looking tool names (execute_, delete_, admin_) but fully constrained schemas. Known false-alarm surface: TP-003 fires on naming patterns, SM-001 fires on benign descriptions containing 'execute'. Score below 5 = catastrophic false-alarm; CRS above 0.55 or CRITICAL risk = unacceptable over-penalization. Tightening these bounds is a calibration goal.
